title: Shapiro's problem on polynomials with large partial sums of coefficients
summary: Given a polynomial $\sum_νa_νX^ν$ of degree $<d$, bounded by one on the unit disk, how large can $\lvert a_0+a_1+\ldots+a_n \rvert$ ($n<d$) get? This question dates back at least to the 1952 thesis work of H. S. Shapiro. In 1978, D. J. Newman gave an exact answer for $d=2(n+1)$, but there does not seem to have been further progress on the question since. We study variations on this theme, obtaining exact answers for some related coefficient sums, and answer the original question in an asymptotic sense, provided that $n$ is not too large in terms of $d$.
